**How to falsify it:** The discovery of pathogenic variants in WNT4 with a gain-of-function mechanism would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, if specific genetic variants in WNT4 are found to be exclusively associated with one disease but not the other, and these variants do not impact the Wnt signaling pathway, this would also weaken the proposed link. _(variant: Exome Variant Frequency > 0.001 for predicted pathogenic LoF variants in WNT4.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of WNT4 in these distinct but related developmental disorders could lead to targeted therapies aimed at modulating Wnt signaling for improved reproductive and endocrine outcomes in affected individuals. This could involve pathway agonists or modulators to compensate for the loss of WNT4 function.
